title: Prompt Caching
markdown:
The Executive system prompt is partitioned for Anthropic prompt caching by `openexecutive.prompts.cache_manager.build_system_blocks`. It emits at most two `cache_control` blocks, consolidated down from four to stay within Anthropic's 4-block API limit alongside the tool definitions and the agent loop's intra-turn marker.

- **Block 0 — persona + knowledge (1h TTL, always present):** the executive persona constant — `EXECUTIVE_PERSONA_PROMPT` for a team, `EXECUTIVE_PERSONA_SOLO_PROMPT` in solo mode — or an admin override, which wins as-is in either mode, with the `{VOICE_PERSONA}` substitution, conditional `WEB_SEARCH_ADDENDUM` / `MCP_ADDENDUM`, the identity addendum (exec name/email, impersonation guard), the timezone addendum, and `KNOWLEDGE_INDEX_SUMMARY`. The timezone addendum names the user's zone, read fresh on every build from the workspace settings (`memory.workspace_settings.get_user_timezone`: the workspace's zone, else `USER_TIMEZONE`, else UTC). Every component is a constant or changes only when an admin or the user changes a setting, so the TTL is long. Setting a new time zone changes the addendum, so the 1h block misses once on that change and is warm again from the next turn — accepted, since a stale zone would mis-schedule follow-ups.
- **Block 1 — company + org (5m TTL, only if non-empty):** `company_profile.to_prompt_block()` plus `render_org_block(mode=…)` — for a team: departments, heads, principals, charters and the People roster; in solo: the principal's own line and their goals grouped by area. Shorter TTL so org edits propagate quickly. The principal's contacts are private to them, so `build_system_blocks(include_contacts=...)` adds the `## Contacts` section, after the team or solo block, only on the principal's own verified turn (`executive._contacts_in_prompt`). That gives block 1 exactly two stable variants per mode — with and without contacts — and never anything per-request; every other turn's block is byte-identical to an install with no contacts.

## Solo mode: one prefix per mode

Solo mode — one person using Open Executive for themselves — changes three cached parts, all resolved **once per turn** by `pin_turn_workspace_mode(session)` (the session's override, else the workspace setting) so they always agree: the block-0 persona, the block-1 org block, and the tool list, which drops `send_company_broadcast`, `send_department_message` and `set_department_head` *before* the sort, so it stays sorted and keeps its 1h marker on the last tool. The resolved mode is pinned on the session for the rest of the turn, so the tool handlers use it too and a switch made mid-turn applies from the next turn. Every part is a constant or stable per install, so each mode keeps its own warm cache and switching modes misses once.

The two personas share most of their text. `prompts/executive_persona.py` holds plain string literals — a shared head, body and tail plus team or solo sections — concatenated at import and never formatted, so both prompts are constants. The team prompt is byte-for-byte what it was before the split; a test pins its sha256.

Tool schemas are static: nothing in a definition depends on company data — `create_goal` takes its area as free text rather than an enum of the current departments, which would change the cached tool prefix every time an area was added. The scheduler's proactive-trigger run (a Session marked `unattended`) is sent the list without `schedule_tools.UNATTENDED_WITHHELD_TOOLS`, so it has a stable tool prefix of its own, as each mode does. Tool definitions are sorted by name so their serialized order is stable across requests; the `web_search` server tool is appended after the sorted list so it never receives a `cache_control` marker. The last client tool carries the third marker (1h TTL).

## The intra-turn marker

The fourth and final breakpoint belongs to the tool-use loop. After each iteration appends its `tool_result` blocks, `executive._apply_loop_cache_marker` moves a single ephemeral marker onto the **newest non-empty tool result**. Without it the loop caches only the static tools+system prefix, so every iteration re-sends the whole accumulated transcript at full input price — the runtime signature is `cache_read_input_tokens` pinned flat while the prompt grows iteration over iteration.

The marker **moves rather than accumulates**: each pass first sweeps every `tool_result` clean, then re-marks the newest one. A marker left in place per iteration would reach `max_iterations` breakpoints and blow the 4-block limit. Sweeping first also makes the helper idempotent — there is no bookkeeping index to drift.

History turns carry **no** marker. A rolling marker on the penultimate assistant turn used to claim a latent fifth breakpoint, which Anthropic rejects outright on the direct path; it never earned its slot, since history turns are flat strings and the system + tool blocks already cover the expensive stable prefix.

**The breakpoint budget, in full:** persona+knowledge (1h) + company+org (5m, conditional) + last client tool (1h) + intra-turn tool result (5m) = at most 4.

RAG context is **never** placed in a cached system block — retrieved hits vary per query and would poison the cache. It is injected into the **user turn** instead.

Specialist calls follow the same rule. Each specialist caches only its static domain prompt (`BaseAgent.analyze`, one ephemeral block); everything per call — retrieved knowledge, failure cases, past decisions, department memory and the company's stage (`<company_stage>`) — goes in the specialist's user turn, so the cached domain prompt is byte-identical across companies and profile edits.

## Tool-result bound

`TOOL_RESULT_MAX_CHARS` (default 50,000) caps a single tool result before it enters the prompt, applied at the one point every result reaches the model rather than at each producer — so it also covers specialist output, tool errors and the unknown-tool fallback, while non-model consumers (the `propose_form_values` JSON parse, the audit trail) still read the full text. It is a circuit breaker, not a routine clipper: the default is set so ordinary tool output never reaches it. A cut result carries an explicit marker naming the tool and stating that the result is incomplete — truncating silently is worse than not truncating, because the model reads the cut text as the whole answer.

**The invariant:** never put dynamic content in a `cache_control` block. A single mutating value breaks the cache and drives roughly a 10x cost increase.
